title: Block: A Set of Seen Values
oneLiner: Walk an array with a set of values seen so far and return the index where a value shows up for the second time.
keyTakeaway: A seen set answers "have I met this before?" in O(1). Check first, then add: the order of those two lines is the whole construct.
explanation:
Return the index of the first element whose value already appeared earlier in the array, or -1 if every value is distinct. In [2, 1, 3, 1, 2] the answer is 3: the second 1 comes before the second 2.

Keep a set of the values you have passed. For each element, ask the set first; if it is there, you have your answer. Only then add the value. The same check-then-add shape is the visited set in BFS and DFS.

starterCode.python:
def first_repeat_index(nums):
    # 1. Make an empty set of values seen so far.
    # 2. Walk the array with its index.
    # 3. If the value is already in the set, return its index.
    # 4. Otherwise add the value to the set.
    # 5. After the loop, return -1.
    return -1

gotchas: Adding the value before checking it, which makes every value look like a repeat.

complexity.note: One pass with O(1) average set lookups; the set can hold all n values when there is no repeat.
